views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the existing Section 301 tariffs in place and use the next Washington round to lock a written memorandum on purchases plus an enforceable mechanism on IP, forced tech transfer, cyber theft, and non-tariff barriers. Do not fire the March 1 List 3 hike to 25% while Liu He is at the table and both sides are reporting progress; be prepared to slide that date if—and only if—text on enforcement is close. Do not pre-commit a tariff rollback or treat Chinese purchase pledges as a substitute for structural commitments, and keep the Huawei/Meng criminal track separate from the trade text.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a mild US opportunity, not a high-cost emergency. The US already covers ~$250B of Chinese imports (Lists 1–2 at 25%, List 3 at 10%) and still holds the unused 10%→25% hike as leverage; Beijing has come back to the table since the G20 truce and is offering larger purchases, while the White House and Xi both described the Feb 14–15 Beijing round as progress toward an MOU even as the official US readout said “much work remains” on structural issues. That is leverage, not existential exposure. The offsetting costs are real but contained: US goods exports to China are down ~17% over the window and China’s 25% soybean tariff plus port-risk aversion cut US soybean shipments to China ~63% Jan–Oct 2018 vs 2017, forcing a $12B USDA aid package and farm-belt political pressure; Michigan sentiment fell from 100.1 (Sep) to 91.2 (Jan) before a partial rebound to 93.8, and industrial production slipped from 104.1 to 102.8. Markets are not pricing crisis (VIX 14.02 on Feb 20 after the December spike; 10-year yield 2.65%). Escalating now would likely stall talks that Trump himself called “not a magical” March 1 deadline and would raise costs on the consumer-heavy List 3 just as companies are already rerouting supply chains. Rolling back without enforcement would repeat the May 19–29 2018 false truce, when purchase talk was followed by the White House restarting 301 actions. Negotiate: hold the current tariff stock, press for a verifiable enforcement snap-back, and only extend the hike if the text is close.
key_factors: Active Feb 2019 talks with reported purchase progress but unresolved IP/enforcement
Unused List 3 hike (10% to 25% on ~$200B) remains the main US bargaining chip
Farm-belt retaliation (soybeans down ~63% to China; $12B USDA aid) is the main US cost
US macro is cooling, not breaking (VIX ~14, sentiment rebound, modest IP dip)
May 2018 purchase-only truce collapsed within days — do not trade rollback for buy pledges
Huawei/Meng criminal track is live and should stay off the trade table

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires: 90-day negotiation window; planned Jan 1 hike of List 3 from 10% to 25% suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou.
Joint statement: China agrees to significantly increase purchases. Mnuchin says trade war is on hold. Truce later collapses on May 29.
Another round of talks through Feb 15. Progress reported on purchases; enforcement mechanism still disputed.
Lighthizer and Mnuchin in Beijing. Purchase commitments discussed; enforcement and structural IP/tech-transfer issues unresolved.
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng; US formally requests extradition.
US exports to China latest $8.08B (Feb 2019) vs $9.73B (Sep 2018), about -17% over the window.
Michigan sentiment 100.1 (Sep) to 91.2 (Jan) then 93.8 (Feb) — down but not collapsing.
VIX 14.02 on 2019-02-20 after December spike to 36 — markets not pricing a crisis.
US industrial production 104.10 (Sep) to 102.84 (Feb) — modest cooling, not a break.
Trump: March 1 is not a magical date. Talks continue in Washington; hike to 25% on $200B still the default without a deal.
Both sides working toward an initial written agreement/MOU; White House says much work remains; Trump open to extending the deadline if close.
US soybean exports to China Jan–Oct 2018 63% lower than 2017; China was >50% of US soybean exports in 2017; USDA $12B trade-aid package.
